chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Husayni narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Isa ibn Abi Maryam al-Ajali informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ziyad al-Azrami narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hatim al-Manqari narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, saying: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) about the Tablet and the Pen.
He said: They are two Angels.

key_terms.اللُّوح: The Tablet, a cosmic record of all things
key_terms.وَالْقَلَم: And the Pen, the instrument of divine writing

ai.seo_question: What are the Tablet and the Pen according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'Tablet' and 'Pen' not as physical instruments but as two distinct angels, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of interpreting cosmic entities as active divine agents. This view emphasizes the continuous, living nature of divine decree (*al-Qada*) and recording (*al-Katb*), distinguishing it from static conceptions of predestination. It underscores the theological principle that creation is sustained through the active obedience of celestial beings who execute God's commands without deviation.
